text.p: British textile group Coats Viyella Plc said on on Thursday that its 1996 results were "disappointing," despite an upturn in some of its markets in the second half.
The company said pre-tax profit plunged 42 percent to 94.4 million pounds ($150.8 million), including expected reorganisation costs of 54.9 million pounds.
The group also announced the reignation of its chief executive Neville Bain.

Coats Viyella, which announced major restructuring plans early in 1996, said cost savings from the reorganisation were likely to exceed the orginal projections of 25 million pounds ($40.14 million) in 1997 and 35 million pounds in 1998.

The company's core thread operations, which supplies thread and yarn for clothing, footwear and cars, picked up in the second half of the year. Home furnishings and fashion retail, which includes the Jaeger and Viyella brands, also showed a "marked improvement."
However the clothing division, which is major supplier to Marks & Spencer Plc and precision engineering, which supplies plastics and metals to industry, both saw operating profits fall.

The company said 1997 would benefit from improved conditions in some markets as well as accelerating cost savings, but added that it was concerned about the impact of sterling's strength on profitability and competitiveness. ($1=.6228 Pound)
